steps.title: The platform

inputs: input | rows | role
`results.coding_alleles` | 38,437 | the callset's coding alleles (allele rows, so one variant with two ALTs is two rows)
`warehouse.coding_annotations` | 38,087 | iteration-2 VEP layer: gene, consequence, impact, gnomAD AF, ClinVar
`warehouse.it2_insilico_annotations` | 38,087 | the same plus AlphaMissense and SpliceAI columns
`warehouse.it2_read_annotations` | 1,199 | the alleles only the raw reads saw ([data-findings §6.3](../../../../ideation/data-findings.md))
Ensembl VEP REST | — | **release 116, assembly GRCh38**, read from the server, not assumed
Row counts are the manifest's own `inputs` block and match
[`ideation/data-findings.md` §6](../../../../ideation/data-findings.md).
**Code.** `mva.zoo.record` / `record_hgvs` / `record_write` (agent *record*, wave 1),
`mva.zoo.types.allele_id` (wave 0). Parameters: `mask_catalogue=false`, `batch_size=200`,
`timeout=300.0`, `base_url=https://rest.ensembl.org`.
### Two fixes this run needed, both measured before being applied
The pass as delivered could not run. Neither failure was in the callset.
**1. `uniprot=1` is not served by the POST endpoint.** The first smoke run died with
`VepError: POST /vep/homo_sapiens/region gave up after 5 attempts (500 server error)`.
A four-cell probe against a **public example variant** (Ensembl's own documentation line, not
this callset) separated the option from the data:
payload | reply
`QUERY_PARAMS` (the annotation pass's set) | **200**, `transcript_consequences[]` carries `hgvsc`, `hgvsp`, `alphamissense`, `spliceai`
`uniprot=1` alone | **500**
`QUERY_PARAMS` + `uniprot=1` | **500**
GET region endpoint, `uniprot=1` | **200**, and `swissprot` + `uniparc` are present
`QUERY_PARAMS` + `protein=1` (POST) | **200**, adds `protein_id` (the Ensembl `ENSP`)
So the option works on **GET** — one variant per request, not a route for 39,286 alleles —
and is unserved on **POST**. Same class of fact as
`annotate_vep.UNAVAILABLE_PARAMS = ("CADD", "LoF")`, which iteration 2 recorded for the same
server. `protein=1` does answer on POST, but returns the `ENSP` accession that `hgvs_p`
already carries as its own prefix, so it buys nothing.
**Fix:** `record_hgvs.EXTRA_PARAMS` is now `{}`, with the measurement in its docstring.
**Consequence, not worked around:** `uniprot` is null for all 39,286 records, and the ESM1b
lane's `ENSP` → UniProt mapping becomes step 2's problem.
**2. The annotation pass's payload times out at 200 alleles.** With `EXTRA_PARAMS` empty the
second smoke run died with `ReadTimeout` on every one of five attempts. `QUERY_PARAMS` asks
for the `AlphaMissense` and `SpliceAI` plugins and two gnomAD frequency joins *per allele* —
none of which this pass reads (`_fill` takes five fields: `transcript`, `hgvsc`, `hgvsp`,
`uniprot`, `consequence`) and all of which are already columns of
`warehouse.it2_insilico_annotations`. Iteration 2's own pass hit the same wall and dropped to
50 alleles and 300 s (`tools/annotate_it2_insilico.py`, whose `--batch-size` help text says
so). **Fix:** `record_hgvs.LEAN_PARAMS = {hgvs, canonical, variant_class}` — `canonical`
because `vep_response.best_transcript` breaks ties on it. The full 200-allele batch then
answered in seconds.
Both fixes are in `src/mva/zoo/record_hgvs.py` and change *what is asked for*, never what is
recorded.
entries.title: One record per allele, and what it can be spelled as

steps.goal: Can every allele in scope be expressed as one normalized record that every model class can read — genomic change, transcript, protein change, DNA window, protein window — with lineage?

hypotheses.author: wave2
hypotheses.prediction: The step-1 run's RunSummary reports p4_1a_fraction >= 0.99 over the coding (non read-only) alleles of results.it4_allele_records.
hypotheses.reasoning: Supersedes revision 2, which recorded the suggested 0.97 because --confidence was omitted while the reasoning stated 0.95; the register is append-only, so the correction is this revision rather than an edit. The number: p4_1a_fraction = 0.99953 against a pre-registered 0.99 threshold, over the whole 38,087-allele coding set, nothing sampled and nothing filtered. Held below the suggested 0.97 because the three evidence rows are not independent — all three are counts off one run of one pass, so the log-odds sum over-credits them. The claim is about spelling only and says nothing about whether any model can score what is spelled (entry 114).
hypotheses.refuted_by: p4_1a_fraction below 0.95 — then the failing consequence class is named from RunSummary.by_consequence and tier-1 coverage is reported per class.
hypotheses.statement: P4-1a: at least 99 % of the callset's coding alleles get a non-null hgvs_p or hgvs_c from the VEP HGVS pass, so one normalized allele record can key every tier-1 model lookup.

entries.title: Four lanes, fetched, licensed, and joined to the record set

steps.goal: Which open models are credible, runnable and licensed for this case, and what is each one's coverage of the record set?

hypotheses.author: wave2
hypotheses.prediction: Each of the four enabled cards in src/mva/zoo/models.toml can be fetched (or is already a warehouse column), is licensed for this use, and joins to results.it4_allele_records so that mva-zoo coverage reports a non-zero scored count for it.
hypotheses.reasoning: All four MVP lanes ran on the real record set inside one day; the two warehouse lanes hit their pre-registered join gates exactly (10,601 and 32,534), REVEL answered live under the field name the card assumed, and ESM1b is MIT, digest-reproduced on two downloads, converted and joined. Held at 0.80 rather than the suggested 0.88 because the claim's word is 'run end-to-end' and ESM1b only does so through a gene-symbol bridge this run had to build, at 29.2 % missense coverage — and because the four lanes needed five measured fixes to get there. Feasibility is established; it was not free. Entry 119.
hypotheses.refuted_by: Any one of the four cannot be fetched, licensed or joined — then that lane is replaced from the opt-A list and the substitution is recorded.
hypotheses.statement: P4-2a: all four MVP lanes (AlphaMissense, ESM1b, SpliceAI, REVEL) run end-to-end on the iteration-4 record set on the laptop in one day.

hypotheses.author: wave2
hypotheses.prediction: For each missense lane that runs, mva-zoo coverage's by-consequence row for missense_variant shows scored/total >= 0.90 of the 15,620 missense alleles in results.it4_allele_records.
hypotheses.reasoning: Both missense tables fall below the 70 % that the plan named as refuting: AlphaMissense 67.9 % (10,601 of 15,620) and ESM1b 29.2 % (4,562 of 15,620). The two misses have different causes and both are reported per consequence class as the refutation clause requires: AlphaMissense is served here from iteration 2's VEP REST plugin pass rather than from the published genome-wide table, so 67.9 % is a property of this delivery and not of the model; ESM1b is keyed on a protein namespace the record set does not carry, and its publisher's gene map reaches only 42.9 % of the genes that carry a missense allele. A new revision is due when a lane is added or when AlphaMissense is fetched as a table. Entry 119.
hypotheses.refuted_by: Any missense table other than EVE covers below 70 % of the callset's missense alleles.
hypotheses.statement: P4-3: every precomputed missense table that runs covers at least 90 % of the callset's missense alleles, EVE excepted (predicted below 30 %).

**Starting state.** `warehouse.allele_scores` was **emptied** before the timing, so the "cold"
in the claim is literal. The append-only `data_lineage` list keeps the edges of the runs that
preceded the reset, including a 52-row REVEL edge whose rows no longer exist — the edge list
records attempts, the table records state, and the two are deliberately not the same thing.
entries.title: Every lane scored, once and only once

steps.goal: Can one batch inference API serve every model through the same contract, cache every score with provenance, and dispatch GPU work without sending more than a sequence window?

hypotheses.author: wave2
hypotheses.prediction: Scoring all four enabled lanes from an empty cache takes <= 3,600 s of wall-clock on this laptop, spends nothing, and every lane writes exactly one warehouse.data_lineage edge named it4-score:<model>.
hypotheses.reasoning: Undecided by its own terms, and recorded as such rather than rounded either way. The cold four-lane pass measured 6,320 s at zero dollars: 1.76x the 3,600 s the claim predicted, and 0.44x the 4 h that was pre-registered as refuting, so neither clause fires. Confidence 0.15 because the number is 76 % over the prediction and the run shows no sign of being unlucky. The refutation clause asks which lane is responsible and it is answered: not a join — the three local lanes finish 47,697 alleles in 53 s — but one serial remote lane, REVEL, at 6,267 s over four attempts against an endpoint that failed three times. Two fixes already took it from about 4.6 h to 1 h 45 m; the third, parallelism (iteration 2 runs three workers on the same service), would put the pass near 35 minutes. That is the revision this claim is owed. Entry 122.
hypotheses.refuted_by: The cold four-lane pass takes more than 4 hours — then the join is profiled and the fix recorded.
hypotheses.statement: P4-4a: a cold MVP run — four lanes over the ~39,300 allele records — completes in at most one hour of laptop wall-clock at zero dollars.
